statements.t: Based on our performance to date and our expectation for the remainder of the year, we are again raising our revenue guidance and cash outlook.”
The Company now expects to end the year with cash and cash equivalents in the range of $53 million to $57 million, versus $49 million to $53 million previously.

The Company’s technology platform creates and screens diverse antibody repertoires and is designed to quickly identify optimal antibodies and other target-binding proteins for its partners’ drug development efforts.

However, OmniAb believes the presentation of actual and projected non-GAAP cash costs and operating expenses, when viewed in conjunction with GAAP figures, provides investors with a more meaningful understanding of our operating performance.

Our technology platform creates and screens diverse antibody repertoires and is designed to quickly identify optimal antibodies and other target-binding proteins for our partners’ drug development efforts.
Our partners can select a biological target to treat a disease and define the properties needed for therapeutic development or use certain of our technologies directly in their own laboratories.

We believe the long-term value of our business will be driven by royalties given that such payments are based on global sales of potential future partner programs, which generally provide for larger and recurring payments as compared to technology access, research and milestone payments.

We believe our revenue will be materially driven by milestone and service revenue from our partnered programs, as well as xPloration platform sales, in the shorter term, and by royalty revenue from our partnered programs in the longer term.

However, there is significant uncertainty in timing and likelihood of reaching marketing authorization in drug discovery and development, and we cannot be certain when, if at all, royalty payments will be a material portion of our revenue.
For so long as the warrants remain out of the money, we do not expect warrant holders to exercise their warrants.
Therefore, any cash proceeds that we may receive in relation to the exercise of such securities will be dependent on the trading price of our common stock.
We anticipate that our principal uses of cash in the future will be primarily to fund our operations, working capital needs, capital expenditures and other general corporate purposes.
